about: Pack s08c (sources/art/s08c, judged in build/reports/s08c-art-landing/details.md; the plan's section 6), cut by build/tools/art/artcut.py. Wave 7B's lines are the clinic and the family (CR1, TC1, the doctor's DW2/DT2/DB2 set, the girl's GZ1-GZ4, the family's NN/MA/AL frames, the waiting room's WR1-WR3); wave 7A's are the Cook lines, each in its own entries. Run with --out to a scratch folder and copy the files the game uses (7B: build/reports/s08-w7b-people-art.md lists them); the numbers go into the game's data where each is wired.

jobs._note: 7B (CLN-23): the pair of crutches lying flat (pads left, feet right, every part down), replacing crutches-flat-belt (B9's crutch turned 90 degrees) under the same name, so data/clinic.json items.crutches needs no change; grey pads on grey: tolerance 4 and no shadow drop (the pads' shaded undersides are dark neutral grey, which the shadow drop took for ground), the gaps between the shafts holes

7B (CLN-196, Zafar 19 Oct: the metal cup, no drop shadow, sitting on the surface): the steel tumbler upright, inside and floor showing; no shadow drawn, so none to drop. Its rim and inside are measured on the cut's alpha into data/clinic/heal/taste.json art.glass

7B (CLN-17; Zafar 20 Oct: likeness yes; 'colour-correct, don't redraw'): the true three-quarter turn to the viewer's left beside the bed, replacing the s08 3q-left set under its file names (s08.cut.json doctor2-3q-left; data/clinic/heal-art.json doctor.views['3q-left'] takes the new numbers); DT2/DB2 are clean edits of DW2 on its own canvas (shift 0,0, skin matched). skin_shift: the whole doctor set (this view and s08's front, 3q-right, waves, poses and box faces) is moved toward his sheet's swatch #C88A6F by one per-pixel Lab shift weighted by skin-likeness, the same function for every file, so every frame and face layer stays matched. artcut.py does not read skin_shift yet: build/reports/s08-w7b-people-art.md has the shift and the request

7B (ART-23): seated front-on for the waiting room's bench, cut like s07.cut.json old-man-sit (the same job shape, fig_h 440, so every bench person is one drawn height: these are drawn 90% of the picture's height, he 80%, and the cut scales each to his height); anchors read off the source by eye (forehead, eyes, mouth, seat = the backs of the thighs on the bench); the colour rung recolours the clothes band in code, as his (heal-art.json waiting.<kind>.tint)
